title: Spuriousness-Aware Meta-Learning for Learning Robust Classifiers

problem.claim: Deep image classifiers can rely on spurious correlations and generalize poorly when those correlations do not hold.

gap.claim: Existing mitigation often requires annotations of spurious correlations, which is a strong practical assumption.

contributions.claim: SPUME is a meta-learning framework for training image classifiers to be robust to spurious correlations.

The framework uses a pre-trained vision-language model to extract text-format image attributes, curates data with varied class-attribute correlations, and introduces a metric for measuring their spuriousness.
The framework meta-trains classifiers on tasks whose support and query sets contain different highly spurious correlations, aiming to learn invariance to those correlations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe SPUME and its spuriousness metric as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the method is robust to spurious correlations without knowing them a priori.
The authors report the best performance on five benchmark datasets across different robustness measures.
The authors report that code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spurious correlations are brittle input-attribute and target associations that image classifiers may exploit.
Robust mitigation is important but commonly depends on spurious-correlation annotations.
The paper proposes SPUME, which iteratively detects and mitigates excessively relied-upon spurious correlations.
A pre-trained vision-language model supplies text-format attributes for curating varied class-attribute correlations and measuring their spuriousness.
Spuriousness-aware meta-learning tasks are used to learn invariance, with reported robustness and benchmark performance gains.

source_observation.claim: The method curates support and query sets with different highly spurious correlations.

interpretation.claim: Training across deliberately shifted nuisance correlations may encourage classifiers to rely less on brittle attributes.

application.claim: For robustness work, construct training tasks that expose controlled variation in suspected nuisance-feature correlations when annotations are unavailable.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy works across domains or shifts beyond the reported benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Text-format attributes extracted by a pre-trained vision-language model are used to curate correlation-varied data.

interpretation.claim: A pretrained multimodal model can provide a practical route to approximate nuisance attributes without direct annotations.

application.claim: Use pretrained representation models to generate candidate attribute descriptions for robustness-oriented data analysis.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify attribute-extraction accuracy, failure cases, or sensitivity to model bias.

unknowns: No quantitative results, baselines, or dataset names are provided.
The abstract does not describe the spuriousness metric, task-construction algorithm, or computational cost.
No limitations or failure cases are reported.
